#
# robots.txt
#
# This file is to prevent the crawling and indexing of certain parts
# of your site by web crawlers and spiders run by sites like Yahoo!
# and Google. By telling these "robots" where not to go on your site,
# you save bandwidth and server resources.
#
# This file will be ignored unless it is at the root of your host:
# Used:    http://example.com/robots.txt
# Ignored: http://example.com/site/robots.txt
#
# For more information about the robots.txt standard, see:
# http://www.robotstxt.org/robotstxt.html

User-agent: *
# CSS, JS, Images
Allow: /core/*.css$
Allow: /core/*.css?
Allow: /core/*.js$
Allow: /core/*.js?
Allow: /core/*.avif
Allow: /core/*.gif
Allow: /core/*.jpg
Allow: /core/*.jpeg
Allow: /core/*.png
Allow: /core/*.svg
Allow: /core/*.webp

Allow: /profiles/*.js$

Allow: /profiles/*.gif
Allow: /profiles/*.jpg
Allow: /profiles/*.jpeg
Allow: /profiles/*.png
Allow: /profiles/*.svg
Allow: /profiles/*.webp

Disallow: /profiles/

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Common Sense shared robots.txt rules.
#
# Scaffolded from cs/shared_modules -> common_files/cs-robots-snippet.txt.
# Do not edit this section in a site repository: it is overwritten on every
# composer install. Change it in the package and release a new version.
#
# Every rule below sits inside its own User-agent group on purpose. A bare
# Disallow here would attach to whichever group the preceding file left open,
# and silently apply to the wrong crawler.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# POLICY: block crawlers that take our content to train models. Allow
# crawlers that show our content to people. Those are three distinct kinds of
# bot, and only the first is a threat to our IP:
#
#   1. TRAINING       collects content to train a model. No reciprocal
#                     benefit to us. -> Disallow.
#   2. SEARCH INDEX   indexes us so we can be surfaced and cited. The
#                     citation links back. -> Allow, deliberately.
#   3. USER-TRIGGERED fetches one page because a person asked to see it.
#                     Builds no index. Blocking it is closer to blocking a
#                     browser than a crawler. -> Allow, deliberately.
#
# Built from Cloudflare AI Crawl Control traffic for commonsense.org, seven
# days to 2026-09-01 -- who actually asks, rather than who we guessed would.
# Categories confirmed against each vendor's own documentation and against
# the ai-robots-txt/ai.robots.txt directory (166 tokens, with an operator,
# function and robots.txt-compliance field per entry) -- NOT against
# Cloudflare's dashboard labels, which are approximate, and whose DISPLAY
# NAMES are not product tokens. "TikTok Spider" is TikTokSpider; "Manus Bot"
# is Manus-User; "Terracotta Bot" is TerraCotta. A token cannot contain a
# space (RFC 9309), so a display name written into this file would match
# nothing while looking perfectly correct -- the CSE-9717 failure exactly.
# See CSE-10472.


# ===========================================================================
# 1. TRAINING CRAWLERS -- observed in our traffic
# ===========================================================================

# Anthropic. ClaudeBot is the current training crawler; anthropic-ai and
# Claude-Web are retired tokens, kept because they cost nothing.
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /
User-agent: anthropic-ai
Disallow: /
User-agent: Claude-Web
Disallow: /

# OpenAI. GPTBot is the training crawler: "used to make our generative AI
# foundation models more useful and safe."
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

# ByteDance. Bytespider is documented as NOT honoring robots.txt, so its
# entry is a statement of intent rather than a control. TikTokSpider is the
# real product token behind what Cloudflare displays as "TikTok Spider".
User-agent: Bytespider
Disallow: /
User-agent: TikTokSpider
Disallow: /

# Meta
User-agent: meta-externalagent
Disallow: /

# Google. Vertex training fetch, distinct from Googlebot.
User-agent: Google-CloudVertexBot
Disallow: /

# Common Crawl. Corpus is widely used as training data.
User-agent: CCBot
Disallow: /

# Huawei
User-agent: PetalBot
Disallow: /

# Timpi
User-agent: Timpibot
Disallow: /

# Amazon. These two collect data for AI applications and both honor
# robots.txt. Amazonbot is deliberately NOT here -- see below.
User-agent: amazon-kendra
Disallow: /
User-agent: bedrockbot
Disallow: /

# Ceramic AI. Real token behind Cloudflare's "Terracotta Bot".
User-agent: TerraCotta
Disallow: /

# Diffbot. Sells extracted page data; its requests carry Diffbot-User. It
# never fetched robots.txt in our traffic, so like Bytespider this states
# intent rather than control.
User-agent: Diffbot
Disallow: /
User-agent: Diffbot-User
Disallow: /


# ===========================================================================
# 2. OPT-OUT TOKENS -- will never appear in traffic, by design
# ===========================================================================
#
# These are not crawlers and no request will ever carry them. Each vendor
# honors the token to exclude us from AI training while its ordinary search
# crawler keeps indexing us. Listing them is the ONLY way to opt out of
# training without also losing search visibility -- which is why they stay
# even though the traffic report shows nothing.

User-agent: Google-Extended
Disallow: /
User-agent: Applebot-Extended
Disallow: /


# ===========================================================================
# 3. RETAINED -- no traffic in the sample, but cheap to keep
# ===========================================================================
#
# Absence over seven days is not proof a crawler is gone; some crawl monthly.
# Keeping a stale entry costs nothing, so these stay until there is a reason.

User-agent: FacebookBot
Disallow: /
User-agent: cohere-ai
Disallow: /
User-agent: omgili
Disallow: /
User-agent: Omgilibot
Disallow: /
User-agent: YouBot
Disallow: /
User-agent: ImagesiftBot
Disallow: /


# ===========================================================================
# DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED
# ===========================================================================
#
# Absence IS the policy here, so it needs saying out loud: an unlisted
# crawler is allowed by default AND stays bound by the site's own
# "User-agent: *" rules. Giving one its own "Allow: /" group would exempt it
# from every site-wide Disallow -- /admin/, /user/*, tracking-parameter URLs
# and the rest -- because named groups and the global group are never
# combined (RFC 9309 s2.2.1). Do not "clarify" this list by adding Allow
# groups. See CSE-10330.
#
# SEARCH INDEX -- they index us in order to cite us, and the citation is a
# link back. Blocking them removes us from the answer engines and protects
# nothing, because none of them train on what they fetch:
#
#   OAI-SearchBot      OpenAI. "Used to surface websites in search results in
#                      ChatGPT's search features." Explicitly not training.
#   PerplexityBot      Perplexity. "Designed to surface and link websites in
#                      search results." Explicitly "not used to crawl content
#                      for AI foundation models."
#   Claude-SearchBot   Anthropic search index.
#   Applebot           Apple's SEARCH crawler -- drives Siri and Spotlight.
#                      NOT the same as Applebot-Extended above, which is the
#                      training opt-out. Blocking Applebot costs us Apple
#                      search visibility and buys no training protection.
#   Amazonbot          Our single largest AI crawler at 22,990 requests in
#                      seven days, more than Googlebot. Documented function is
#                      "service improvement and enabling answers for Alexa
#                      users" -- not training. Amazon's data-collection
#                      crawlers are amazon-kendra and bedrockbot, both blocked
#                      above. Honors robots.txt.
#
# USER-TRIGGERED -- a person asked to see one of our pages. No index is
# built, nothing is retained. Note also that several vendors state these
# fetches fall outside robots.txt, so blocking them may achieve nothing:
#
#   ChatGPT-User       OpenAI. "Not used for crawling the web in an automatic
#                      fashion. Because these actions are initiated by a
#                      user, robots.txt rules may not apply."
#   Perplexity-User    "Not used for web crawling or to collect content for
#                      training AI foundation models."
#   Claude-User        Anthropic, fetching on a user's behalf.
#   DuckAssistBot      DuckDuckGo.
#   MistralAI-User     Mistral.
#   Meta-ExternalFetcher
#   Manus-User         Real token behind Cloudflare's "Manus Bot", 1,270
#                      requests. Operator Butterfly Effect. Acts for a human
#                      user completing a task.
#   Amzn-User          Amazon, fetching to answer a user's Alexa query.
#
# One honest gap: OpenAI states plainly that OAI-SearchBot content is not
# used for training, but says nothing either way about ChatGPT-User. If we
# ever want a reason to block that one, the silence is it.


# ===========================================================================
# OPEN -- do not add these without a decision
# ===========================================================================
#
#   cohere-ai          Blocked above, but the directory describes it as
#                      "retrieves data to provide responses to user-initiated
#                      requests" -- category 3, not training. No traffic in
#                      the sample, so low stakes either way. Reclassify?
#
#   PetalBot           Blocked above. "Used to provide recommendations in
#                      Huawei assistant" is assistant-serving rather than
#                      training, so it sits on the line. 351 requests.
#
#   YouBot             "Scrapes data for search engine and LLMs" -- genuinely
#                      both. Blocking costs us You.com search presence.

# robots-additions.txt
# Site rules, appended after core and the cs/shared_modules AI-crawler
# snippet. Keep the User-agent line: the snippet ends inside a bot's group.

User-agent: *

# Paths (clean URLs)
Disallow: /user/*
Disallow: /users/*
Disallow: /bio/*
Disallow: /es/usuarios
Disallow: /es/usuario/*
Disallow: /es/buscar

# Pagination
Allow: /*/sitemap.xml?page=
Disallow: /*?page=

# PDFs
Allow: /*.pdf$
Disallow: /*.pdf?
# Reviews blocked
Disallow: /movie-reviews/xxx
Disallow: /movie-reviews/xxx/user-reviews/*
Disallow: /movie-reviews/sexy-baby-educational-version
Disallow: /movie-reviews/sexy-baby-educational-version/user-reviews/*
# User Review Comments Manage Links
Disallow: /*/user-reviews/manage/

# Search/Sort/Filter Params
